title: Using Design of Experiments to Optimize CryoEM Grids for Membrane Proteins
content: The process of optimizing grids for cryoEM remains a significant bottleneck due to the highly specific and often unpredictable freezing parameters required for each sample. In general, there is a need to approach the grid optimization process more strategically and efficiently to limit resources and microscope time required. Membrane proteins, whose structural studies are of high importance to biochemistry and biomedicine, are particularly challenging to optimize as they often require the addition of detergents for structural preservation, protection against denaturation at the air water interface (AWI), and to prevent or reduce preferred orientation. Multiple potential complications can arise in the process of optimizing freezing conditions for membrane proteins in addition to the general difficulties of CryoEM grid optimization. The selection of the best detergent to use for a particular sample is often only achievable through extensive trial-and-error. If a sample behaves reasonably well without detergent, but high-resolution single particle analysis (SPA) reveals significant preferred orientation, the process of grid optimization must be redone from the beginning, as optimized parameters such as sample concentration and blot time can significantly change when detergents are added.
